paragraphs: Cylus makes cybersecurity software for railways, built to continuously monitor, detect, and protect every layer of rail operational technology. Its product, CylusOne, covers mainline, urban, and freight rail operations.

The system integrates passively into an operator's network and existing monitoring tools. It automatically discovers and classifies all assets in the operational networks. Vulnerabilities are prioritized and scored by analyzing their severity in the rail environment. Detection runs continuously using deep packet inspection and machine learning to identify and classify threats across railway and IT protocols. Coverage reaches trackside and wayside networks, train-to-ground communications, operational control and maintenance centers, and station networks.

The company says the product lets operators prove compliance with frameworks including IEC 62443-3-2, NIST 800-82, and EN TS 50701. It describes CylusOne as the first rail cybersecurity solution certified to IEC 62443-4-2 at Security Level 3. Cylus says it works with technology providers, integrators, and rail experts worldwide. For passenger rail, detection is tuned to separate expected supervision and control traffic in ERTMS environments from anomalous behavior.

quote.text: CylusOne enables teams to investigate and contain threats without disrupting service, integrates with existing SOC processes, and keeps freight rail operations at the center of decision-making.
